newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha recovers with crude, wet trade stays down.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha recovers with crude, wet trade stays down.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended slightly higher on Monday after crude oil bounced higher, but cash deals were scarce and freight rates inhibited trades out of the Med.
One end-user was seen bidding $224 cif NWE for 25,000 tonnes of either Algerian or Egyptian material, to be delivered by end-January, sources said.
The same end-user was seen as a buyer on Friday at $220, so the higher bid buoyed the market, though a final deal for today's bid was not confirmed.
Cargo prices therefore were notionally valued at $220/$224 cif NWE with the Med $4 lower.
Swaps for the rest of January were heard roughly up $1 at $220/$222 a tonne with Feb holding a $3 backwardation at $217/$218.
One source said sellers of high paraffinic material or 25,000 tonne cargoes were able to find buyers, but they had more difficulty for paper spec quality and heavier napthenic and aromatic grades.
"The problem is the small parcels," he said.
